sections.heading: C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A24
The windshield and windows forward of or beside the driver may not have one-way glass, film or another treatment that reduces light transmission below 35 percent. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A24
For rear-window glazing, the handbook prohibits light transmission below 20 percent and states an enforcement tolerance of 9 percent. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A24
A windshield sunscreen device must not obstruct or reduce the driver’s clear view. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A24
The handbook prohibits extending film below the AS-1 line or below the lowest point of the sun visor. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A24
Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with paper or cloth towels because glare on dirty glass makes seeing harder. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A24
Keep washer fluid topped up and use antifreeze washer fluid when temperatures may fall below freezing. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A24
Clean inside window surfaces because smoking can leave a film on the glass. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A24
Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from all windows and clean the vehicle’s front, sides and back. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A24
Do not hang objects from the mirror or crowd the windshield with decals that can block the view. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A24
Keep headlights, reverse lights, brake lights and taillights clean because dirty lenses can reduce their light by 50 percent. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A25
Sit upright with the back against the seat and feet on the floor because slouching can reduce restraint effectiveness. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A25
Adjust the seat and mirrors before driving to obtain a clear view, full pedal and steering control, and room for the air bag. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A25
The driving position should allow the foot to pivot between brake and accelerator while the heel stays on the floor. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A25
The steering-wheel top should stay at or below shoulder height and below the chin. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A25
Keep 10 inches between the chest and steering wheel without moving the seat so far forward that steering becomes difficult or reclining the seat. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A25
Set the head restraint to touch the back of the head at a height no lower than the ears to help prevent whiplash. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A25
Adjust the inside mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind the vehicle. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A25
Set a day-and-night mirror for the time of day in which you are driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A25
Set outside mirrors for maximum side and rear visibility and fewer blind spots. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A25
To set the left outside mirror using the handbook’s method, rest the head against the closed window and adjust the mirror until the vehicle’s edge is barely visible. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A25
To set the right mirror, lean until the head is below the inside mirror or above the center console, then adjust until the right vehicle edge is barely visible. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A25
With that outside-mirror setup, the vehicle sides will not appear during ordinary mirror glances and each side gains 12 to 16 degrees of viewing area. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A25
Always fasten the driver’s seatbelt and ensure passengers use belts or child restraints. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A25
Seatbelts reduce injury and death risk, help prevent ejection and help the driver retain control in a crash. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A25
South Dakota law prohibits driving or riding in the front seat without a seatbelt. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A25
Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and shoulder with little or no slack, never under an arm or behind the back. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A25
A misrouted shoulder belt can cause serious internal injury in a crash. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A25
Fasten the lap belt snugly and low over the hips to reduce the risk of sliding out during a crash. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A25
Use seatbelts even when the vehicle has air bags. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A25
The handbook describes air bags as protection from striking the steering wheel, dashboard or windshield, while warning that they do not provide the cited side, rear or rollover protection or keep the driver behind the wheel in those situations. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0025]

ranked.label: Pedagogic emphasis: Inspect roadworthiness and visibility, then set driving position and restraints.
